pattern.crimePattern: sacco treasurer kills the CEO who found ghost-member loans, then walks out in the victim's coat to fake a later sighting
pattern.notes: Fictional sacco on a real street. Ghost members and irregular loans in savings co-operatives are a recurring, widely reported problem; no real sacco, officer or regulator decision is depicted.

ob.reportedBy: Cleaner, Rift Walimu Sacco, Kenyatta Avenue, Nakuru
ob.text: A cleaner reports the chief executive of Rift Walimu Sacco, Ezra Kamande (45), found dead in the sacco's strong room on Kenyatta Avenue, Nakuru, at 07:30. The night askari states that the CEO left the building at 21:00 the previous night.

people.name: Ezra Kamande
people.bio: Runs a teachers' savings and loans co-operative. Known all over town for his long camel coat and grey felt hat.

facts.text: Ezra Kamande, CEO of Rift Walimu Sacco, was found dead in the sacco's strong room at 07:30.
The night askari says the CEO left the building at 21:00 the previous night.
Ezra lay between the loan-file shelves in the strong room, struck on the head.
The sacco's heavy brass commemorative paperweight lay on the strong-room floor. It has rounded edges.
Ezra's camel coat and grey hat hang on the hook behind his office door.
In the coat pocket: a chemist's receipt, 21:05, blood-pressure tablets, sacco member discount, 'Member 0114 — K. Muthuri'.
Askari's log: '21:00 — Mr Kamande out (coat & hat).'
Lemaron was at the front door from 18:00 to 06:00; his log has an entry every hour.
Eunice: in eighteen years Ezra ate supper at home at eight every night. Last night he never came.
Eunice: he called at 17:50: "I'll be late. I have to deal with Kirimi."
Eunice was at home with the children all evening, waiting for him.
Strong room: 41 loan files, KSh 18 million in all. Every approval is signed K. Muthuri.
Members' register: 17 of the 41 borrowers are on the deceased-members list. The other 24 have ID numbers that belong to nobody.
Ezra's draft letter to the board and the co-operatives regulator: '41 irregular loans approved by the treasurer.' To go on Tuesday morning.
The back door opens only with a board member's key (five exist). The bolt the cleaner shot at 18:30 was found drawn back in the morning.
Rose: she shoots the back-door bolt at 18:30 every night. Only someone with a board key could open it from outside after that.
Records, Kirimi's line: Nakuru CBD mast 17:40–21:30, then Milimani, where he lives.
Records: PesaPap, 21:05, the chemist on Kenyatta Avenue.
Club register and bill: W. Cheruiyot signed in at 17:15 for drinks, then dinner 18:00–22:30, bill signed at 22:28. Thirty diners.
Counter incident book: last week member J. Mumbi, with a defaulted loan, shouted threats at the CEO.
Hellen: Jemimah served customers in her shop next door until she closed at 20:00; they sat on the bench together at 19:00.
Board minutes: the sacco's land purchase was approved unanimously last year.
Board minutes: salaries reviewed and agreed; no disputes recorded.
Kirimi gives his fingerprints voluntarily, confidently.
Autopsy: a single blow to the head with a heavy object with a rounded edge.
Autopsy: death between 17:30 and 19:30. Lunch partly digested, and no supper.
Autopsy: no signs of suffocation, poisoning or heart failure.
Dr. Chebii, on site: the wound is consistent with the brass paperweight.
Lab: Kirimi's prints are on the paperweight. He is on the board and handles it often: not decisive on its own.
Lemaron: "Mr Kamande came out at nine in his coat and hat, and waved."
Lemaron, asked again: he didn't see the face under the hat brim. "He walked a bit bent. Mr Kamande walks very straight. But it was late."
Kirimi: "I left the office at five and was home in Milimani by half past."
Kirimi: "Ezra left at nine. The askari saw him."
Kirimi admits he stayed late "on some files", went to the chemist and went home. He says he didn't see Ezra after five.
Wilfred: "I was at the club dinner."
Wilfred: "Nobody questions the treasurer. He was here before any of us."
Jemimah: "I was at my shop, then home."

interrogations.intro: Kirimi folds his hands on the board-room table. "Terrible. Terrible. I left at five. The askari saw Ezra go at nine."

topics.reply: Every loan goes through committee. I sign what the committee recommends.
Take my prints. I have nothing to hide. I hold that paperweight at every board meeting.

interrogations.intro: Lemaron stands at attention by his stool. "I saw him go. Nine o'clock. The coat, the hat. He waved."

topics.reply: Every hour I write. I wrote him out at nine.

interrogations.intro: Eunice sits with her hands around a cup she hasn't drunk. "He ate at eight. Every night of our marriage."

topics.reply: At ten to six he called. "I'll be late, I have to deal with Kirimi." Those were the words.

interrogations.intro: Wilfred has come from the club in yesterday's suit. "I know how this looks. The deputy. Ask me."

topics.reply: Nobody questions the treasurer. He was here before any of us. Before the building.

interrogations.intro: Jemimah keeps her apron on. "I shouted. I owe them money. I don't kill people."

topics.reply: Ask Hellen next door. We sat on the bench together.

contradictions.reaction: Lemaron frowns for a long time. "...I didn't see his face. The hat. He walked a bit bent. Mr Kamande walks very straight. But it was late. It was his coat."
I stayed late on some files. I went to the chemist and I went home. I didn't see Ezra after five.

prosecutor.pass: His member number in the dead man's coat, his phone in town until half nine, his signature on 41 ghost loans. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. The deputy was signing a dinner bill in front of thirty people. Who was wearing that coat?
No. The askari didn't lie, but he didn't see a face. Whose tablets are in the pocket?

prosecutor.pass: One blow, a rounded brass edge, before half past seven. Yes.
fail: He was dead before supper. He never came back to the office late.
Dr. Chebii found a blow, not suffocation.

prosecutor.pass: Seventeen dead members and twenty-four who never lived, all signed by the treasurer. That's the reason.
fail: The land purchase was unanimous. That isn't it.
That ambition belongs to a man at a club dinner.

proof.concludes: Ezra died between 17:30 and 19:30, before his unbroken eight o'clock supper. He couldn't have walked out at 21:00. The askari saw a coat and a hat, not a face: someone else was wearing them.
Whoever wore the coat at 21:00 bought blood-pressure tablets at 21:05 on Kirimi Muthuri's member number, then hung the coat back on Ezra's hook.

Kirimi said he was home by 17:30; his phone stayed in town until 21:30 and paid the chemist at 21:05. He admits staying late. The back door, which only a board key opens, was used after the 18:30 bolt.

Ezra had found 41 ghost loans approved by Kirimi and was reporting them in the morning; at 17:50 he said he had "to deal with Kirimi". Kirimi Muthuri struck him with the brass paperweight in the strong room, because Ezra had found the ghost-member loans.

eliminations.why: Wilfred signed in at the club at 17:15 and was at dinner until 22:30, in front of thirty diners.
Jemimah was serving in her shop until 20:00, with her neighbour beside her; and she has no back-door key.
Lemaron was at the front door all night; honest, and mistaken.
Eunice was at home with the children, waiting for him.
He was dead before 19:30; he never came back late.
A blow to the head, not suffocation.
That ambition is Wilfred's, and he was at the club dinner.
That debt is Jemimah's, and she was in her shop.
No salary dispute was ever recorded.

reconstruction.text: Ezra goes through the loan book and finds 41 loans, KSh 18 million, to members who are dead or never existed. Every approval: K. Muthuri.
17:50. He calls home: "I'll be late, I have to deal with Kirimi." In the strong room he shows Kirimi the files. In the morning the letter goes to the board and the regulator.
The brass paperweight. Kirimi locks the strong room and waits in his office for the building to empty.
21:00. In the dim lobby a man in the famous camel coat and grey hat walks past the askari, a little bent, and waves. At 21:05 he buys his blood-pressure tablets on his own member number.
He comes back through the back door with his board key, hangs the coat and hat on Ezra's hook and leaves again. The receipt stays in the pocket.

clockPlan.note: No detention needed. The prints result (6 h) teaches that prints can be innocent; it isn't needed to charge.

ui.beatNotes: A witness who isn't lying but is wrong. Lemaron's statement gets a third mark, neither red nor grey: an amber "mistaken" mark once the time of death is set against it. The notebook now distinguishes lies, innocent lies and honest mistakes. Mwalimu, after: "People see the coat. Detectives see who's inside it."
